mainTopic: The end of the משנה about twin firstborn animals, and the גמרא's question of whether people (not just nature) can make something exact (צמצום).
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה about a ewe that gives birth to two males at once. The משנה covers the priestly gifts (מתנות), the case where one twin died, and the case of a male and a female. Then the גמרא begins. The school of רבי ינאי explains that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that exactness (צמצום) is possible even in natural events, so it is surely possible for human actions. The רבנן hold that nature cannot be exact, and the גמרא asks what they hold about human actions. It tries several proofs: the red line around the מזבח, the measurements of the vessels and the מזבח, a טמא clay oven split into equal halves, and רבי אליעזר's ruling about a body found exactly between two towns. Each proof is rejected in turn. The last rejection begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second twin and the priestly gifts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the owner who keeps the doubtful second twin must give the מתנות when he slaughters it. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is obligated in the gifts, and רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: We join the משנה in the middle. The doubtful second twin stays with the owner. The תנא קמא says the owner must still give the כהן the מתנות (foreleg, jaw, and maw).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second animal might be a בכור and might not be, so it is a ספק. The תנא קמא says that the gifts still apply to this doubtful animal. רבי יוסי says the owner is exempt, and the גמרא explains his reason later (as רש״י notes).

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly gifts from a slaughtered non-sacred animal: foreleg, jaw, and maw

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the priestly gifts,
phrases.notes: Refers to the doubtful second twin, which stays with the owner

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the doubtful second twin is obligated in מתנות. רבי יוסי: it is exempt.

steps.title: When one of the twins died
steps.stepSummary: If one twin died, רבי טרפון says the כהן and the owner split the survivor. רבי עקיבא says the one trying to take must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says they divide. רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: one of the two males died, and we don't know if it was the בכור. Two opinions are given on what happens to the survivor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון splits the doubt down the middle. רבי עקיבא applies the general rule of המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה. The כהן is the one trying to take, so without proof the owner keeps the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take from another must bring proof

steps.whyThisMatters: המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה is one of the most basic rules of monetary doubt across all of ש״ס.

phrases.english: If one of them died —
Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide it,
phrases.notes: The כהן and the owner split the remaining animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
the one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: split the survivor. רבי עקיבא: the owner keeps it unless the כהן brings proof.

steps.title: Twins that are a male and a female
steps.stepSummary: If the twins were a male and a female, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A male and a female: the כהן has nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the case of a male and a female born together. Everyone agrees the כהן receives nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The female may have come out first and 'opened the womb.' If so, the male is not a בכור. Since the כהן cannot prove otherwise, he has no claim.

phrases.english: A male and a female —
the priest has nothing here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a final case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a male and female born together, the כהן receives nothing.

steps.title: The two views on exactness in natural events
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי explains the dispute in the משנה. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that natural events can coincide exactly, so human actions surely can. The רבנן hold that natural events cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: We have heard that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds it is possible to be exact in things done by Heaven, and all the more so in things done by people. The רבנן hold it is impossible to be exact in things done by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by spelling out what each side in the משנה believes about צמצום, meaning perfect exactness. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי says two births can happen at exactly the same moment. That is a natural event, done 'by Heaven.' If nature can be exact, then deliberate human action surely can be. The רבנן deny that nature is ever exact, which leaves open what they think about humans.

keyTerms.meaning: To be perfectly exact, so that two things match precisely
By the hands of Heaven, meaning natural events
By human hands, meaning deliberate human action
The school (study house) of רבי ינאי

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן's position here only covers natural events. Do not assume they also say humans cannot be exact. That is exactly the open question.

phrases.english: GEMARA
They said in the school of Rabbi Yannai:
Regarding Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, we have heard of him
that he says it is possible to be exact in the hands of Heaven,
phrases.notes: Twins can be born at exactly the same instant

phrases.english: and all the more so in human hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן — בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: and the Rabbis — in the hands of Heaven it is impossible to be exact,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by explaining the principle behind the משנה's opening dispute (on the previous amud) between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the רבנן over twins whose heads emerged together. This is not the רבי יוסי of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי: exactness is possible in nature, and certainly by people. רבנן: it is impossible in nature.

steps.title: What do the רבנן hold about human exactness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן think people can be exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the main question of this passage. This question drives the attempted proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perhaps the רבנן agree that a person, acting on purpose, can be perfectly exact. Or perhaps they hold that even people can never be perfectly exact.

phrases.english: In human hands, what [is their view]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the open question left by step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, can a human action be perfectly exact?

steps.title: Proof from the red line around the altar
steps.stepSummary: The red line marked the exact middle of the מזבח. If people could not be exact, blood would sometimes land on the wrong half. So people must be able to be exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A red line went around the middle of the altar, to separate the upper bloods from the lower bloods. If you say people cannot be exact, sometimes the כהן would put upper blood below and lower blood above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first proof that people can be exact. The proof comes from the חוט של סיקרא, the red line around the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood must be sprinkled above the middle of the מזבח and some below it. The line is meant to mark the exact midpoint. If humans cannot measure exactly, the line would be slightly off, and blood would end up in the wrong zone.

keyTerms.meaning: The red line painted around the altar
Blood that goes on the upper half
Blood that goes on the lower half

phrases.english: Come and hear:
a red line encircles it in the middle,
to separate between the upper bloods
and the lower bloods.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם בִּידֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: And if you say it is impossible to be exact in human hands,
sometimes he would put the upper ones below
and the lower ones above!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 5
steps.raayaObject: That people can be perfectly exact
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מדות about the red line marking the middle of the מזבח

steps.title: The line was made a bit wider
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails, because the line was made slightly wide so that it surely covered the true middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they widen it a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the red line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line does not need to hit the exact midpoint. It is made a bit thick, so the real middle falls somewhere inside it. The כהן sprinkles clearly above or below the line, so no exact measurement is needed.

phrases.english: Because one widens it a little.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the red-line proof. The question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The line's width solves the problem without any exact measurement.

steps.title: Proof from the measurements of the vessels and altar
steps.stepSummary: The תורה gives exact measurements for the משכן vessels and the מזבח. This suggests that people can measure exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the measurements of the vessels, from the measurements of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof. The proof comes from the exact sizes the תורה commands for the vessels and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה would not command exact measurements unless people could actually build them exactly. So human צמצום should be possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The measurements of the vessels of the משכן/מקדש

phrases.english: Come and hear from the measurements of the vessels,
from the measurements of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attempt to answer step 5 after the first proof failed
steps.raayaObject: That people can be perfectly exact
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact measurements the תורה gives for the vessels and the מזבח

steps.title: Do your best, and it is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. For the vessels, the תורה only asks us to do our best, and whatever we can do is pleasing to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the Merciful One said 'Make it,' and however you are able to make it is pleasing to Him: 'All this in writing, from the hand of ה׳ upon me, He made me understand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof. It explains that the measurements of the vessels do not require true perfection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ commanded us to build the vessels and accepts our best effort, even if it is not perfectly exact. So the exact measurements prove nothing about whether humans can achieve true צמצום. The verse from דברי הימים shows that the plans came from ה׳ and that people build them as well as they can.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that people can be exact were rejected. The red line was widened, and the vessels only need our best effort. So far, the question of the רבנן's view on human צמצום remains open.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the Merciful One said: make it,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכֹל הֵיכִי דְּמָצֵית לְמִיעְבַּד נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and in whatever way you are able to make it, it is pleasing to Him,
"All this in writing, from the hand of the Lord upon me, He made me understand."

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the vessels/altar proof. The question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vessels require best effort, not true precision, so they prove nothing about human צמצום.

steps.title: The split clay oven: exact halves are impossible
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא cites a ברייתא: a טמא clay oven split into two equal pieces leaves both pieces טמא, because it is impossible to be exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: Come and hear a proof. If someone split a טמא clay oven into two pieces and the pieces look equal, both pieces stay טמא, because it is impossible to make them exactly equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא brings a new proof, this time showing that people cannot measure exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken clay vessel becomes טהור only in its smaller piece, while the bigger piece stays טמא. If the two pieces truly could be exactly equal, neither would count as the 'bigger' piece. The ברייתא says both are טמא because we assume one is secretly bigger, which means exact equality is impossible even when a person does the dividing.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula for bringing a proof from a source
He divided it into two pieces
It is impossible to be exactly precise

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier proofs (Steps 6 and 8) tried to show that people CAN be exact. This proof points in the opposite direction: that people CANNOT be exact.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said: Come and hear:
If one divided it into two, and they are equal,
phrases.notes: Refers to a טמא clay oven or vessel.

phrases.english: both of them are impure,
because it is impossible to be exactly precise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof on the question from Step 5, arguing the opposite side from Steps 6 and 8.
steps.raayaObject: That people cannot measure exactly, even when a person does the dividing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a טמא clay oven split into two equal pieces.

steps.title: Clay is different because of its bumps
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rejects the proof: broken clay has uneven edges, so it is uniquely hard to measure exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: A clay vessel is different, because it has little dents and bumps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא knocks down רב קטינא's proof by saying the clay case is a special exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jagged, bumpy edge of broken clay makes it impossible to measure each half exactly. That says nothing about ordinary measuring, which may well be exact. So the ברייתא proves only that clay is hard to measure, not that people can never be exact.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: the formula for limiting a source to its own special case
Dents or indentations: an uneven surface

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
An earthenware vessel is different,
since it has indentations in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: שָׁאנֵי כְּלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 10 by limiting it to clay.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The ברייתא no longer shows anything about measuring in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling depends on the bumpy nature of broken clay, not on a general rule that measuring cannot be exact.

steps.title: A body found exactly between two towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי אליעזר: if a body is found exactly between two towns, both towns bring a עגלה ערופה. It then asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a dead body was found exactly between two towns, both towns bring two heifers. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about the עגלה ערופה and asks why רבי אליעזר rules this way. It is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the single town closest to the body brings a עגלה ערופה. רבי אליעזר says that when the body lies exactly in the middle, both towns bring one. The question 'what is his reason?' prepares the inference that people can measure exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly lined up, precisely in the middle
Heifers, here meaning the עגלה ערופה

phrases.english: Come and hear: If it was found precisely
between two towns,
the two of them bring two heifers;
this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצָא מְכוּוָּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clay proof fails, the גמרא brings a new source pointing the other way: that people can be exact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוטה about a עגלה ערופה when the body is found between two towns.

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר holds people can be exact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר holds that measuring done by people can be exact, and that the word 'nearest' can include two equally near towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not because he holds that when people do the measuring, it is possible to be exact? And he holds that the word 'nearest' in the פסוק can even mean two 'nearest' towns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: רבי אליעזר's ruling only makes sense if people can measure exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling rests on two ideas. First, people's measuring can be exact, so the two distances truly can be equal. Second, the singular word 'הקרובה' in the פסוק can apply to two towns that are equally near. If exact measuring were impossible, the towns would share one heifer with a condition about which town is really closer, not bring two.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not because...? The formula for proposing the reason behind a ruling
By human hands, meaning done by people
Nearest: the word in the פסוק about the town that brings the עגלה ערופה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clearest attempt so far to show from a תנא's ruling that people can measure exactly.

phrases.english: Is it not because he holds:
by human hands it is possible to be exactly precise,
and 'nearest' even includes two nearest towns?
phrases.notes: The פסוק (דברים כ״א:ג) uses the singular 'הקרובה,' and רבי אליעזר reads it to include two equally near towns.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר בִּידֵי אָדָם אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is the reason' of Step 12 and completes the proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling that two towns each bring a heifer.

steps.title: The proof from רבי אליעזר is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof: 'No, רבי אליעזר...' The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to push back on the proof from רבי אליעזר. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לא' signals that the proof will fail. The גמרא is about to give a different reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling, one that does not depend on people being able to measure exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the opening word of a rejection

phrases.english: No, Rabbi Eliezer
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to reject the proof of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי אליעזר. The details follow on the next amud.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated on this amud. The גמרא will offer another reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling.
